subproblems.title: Real-integral form of a lower-integral Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev inequality (parent step 0)
subproblems.statement: Let P be a natural number, p > 0 a real number and C ≥ 0 a real constant (an element of NNReal, viewed in [0, ∞] in the hypothesis). Write L^P = volume on R^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), ∫⁻ for the lower Lebesgue integral with values in [0, ∞], ‖t‖ₑ ∈ [0, ∞] for the extended norm and |Dw(x)| for the operator norm of the derivative. Assume (H): every C¹ function w : R^P → R with compact support satisfies ∫⁻ ‖w(x)‖ₑ^p dL^P(x) ≤ C · (∫⁻ ‖Dw(x)‖ₑ dL^P(x))^p. Then there is a real number c > 0 such that every C¹ function w : R^P → R with compact support satisfies (∫ |w|^p dL^P)^{1/p} ≤ c ∫ |Dw| dL^P, with Bochner integrals and real powers (the power 1/p is written p⁻¹).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (C : NNReal), 0 < p → (∀ w : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 w → HasCompactSupport w → ∫⁻ x, ‖w x‖ₑ ^ p ≤ (C : ℝ≥0∞) * (∫⁻ x, ‖fderiv ℝ w x‖ₑ) ^ p) → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 w → HasCompactSupport w → (∫ z, |w z| ^ p) ^ p⁻¹ ≤ c * ∫ z, ‖fderiv ℝ w z‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 0. Mathlib's GNS inequality (Mathlib/Analysis/FunctionalSpaces/SobolevInequality.lean, `lintegral_pow_le_pow_lintegral_fderiv`) replaces Simon's citation of [GT01] in the Sobolev step of Ch. 3, 4.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 689–712). Its conclusion has exactly the shape of hypothesis (H). The parent supplies (H) from that Mathlib theorem. This child performs the parent's 'routine bookkeeping between lintegral and the real integral' and the choice c := c₀ + 1 > 0. It uses no import beyond the contract's.

Fix P, p > 0, C ≥ 0 and (H). Write L := L^P.

1. Constant. Put c := C^{1/p} + 1, where C^{1/p} is the real power of the real number C ≥ 0. Then c ≥ 1 > 0. It depends only on C and p. Now fix a C¹ function w : R^P → R with compact support, and set K := tsupport w, a compact set.

2. The derivative term. w is C¹, so w and Dw are continuous. Dw vanishes outside K: w ≡ 0 on the open set R^P \ K, so Dw = 0 there (HasCompactSupport.fderiv). Thus Dw is continuous with compact support, hence L-integrable. In particular A := ∫⁻ ‖Dw‖ₑ dL < ∞, and ∫ |Dw| dL = A.toReal (integral_norm_eq_lintegral_enorm; Dw is a.e. strongly measurable because it is continuous).

3. The function term. Since p > 0, t ↦ t^p is continuous on [0, ∞). So x ↦ |w(x)|^p is continuous and nonnegative, hence a.e. strongly measurable. Therefore ∫ |w|^p dL = (∫⁻ ofReal(|w|^p) dL).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae). For every x, ofReal(|w(x)|^p) = ofReal(|w(x)|)^p = ‖w(x)‖ₑ^p, by ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg (|w(x)| ≥ 0, p ≥ 0) and ‖w(x)‖ₑ = ofReal ‖w(x)‖ = ofReal |w(x)|. Hence ∫ |w|^p dL = (∫⁻ ‖w‖ₑ^p dL).toReal.

4. Passing to real numbers. The right side C · A^p of (H) for w is finite: C is a finite constant, and A^p < ∞ because A < ∞ and p ≥ 0. ENNReal.toReal is monotone when the larger value is finite (ENNReal.toReal_mono). So (H) gives (∫⁻ ‖w‖ₑ^p dL).toReal ≤ (C · A^p).toReal = C · (A.toReal)^p (ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_rpow, ENNReal.coe_toReal). By steps 2 and 3, ∫ |w|^p dL ≤ C (∫ |Dw| dL)^p.

5. Taking the 1/p power. Put I := ∫ |Dw| dL ≥ 0. Both sides of step 4 are ≥ 0, and t ↦ t^{1/p} is monotone on [0, ∞) since 1/p > 0. Hence (∫ |w|^p dL)^{1/p} ≤ (C I^p)^{1/p} = C^{1/p} (I^p)^{1/p} = C^{1/p} I. Here Real.mul_rpow applies to C ≥ 0 and I^p ≥ 0, and Real.rpow_rpow_inv applies to I ≥ 0 and p ≠ 0. Since I ≥ 0, C^{1/p} I ≤ (C^{1/p} + 1) I = c I. This is (∫ |w|^p dL)^{1/p} ≤ c ∫ |Dw| dL. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose c := C^{1/p} + 1 > 0.
For C¹ compactly supported w, Dw is continuous with compact support: ∫⁻‖Dw‖ₑ < ∞ and ∫|Dw| = (∫⁻‖Dw‖ₑ).toReal.
|w|^p is continuous and nonnegative, so ∫|w|^p = (∫⁻‖w‖ₑ^p).toReal.
Take toReal of (H), whose right side is finite: ∫|w|^p ≤ C(∫|Dw|)^p.
Take the 1/p power: (∫|w|^p)^{1/p} ≤ C^{1/p}∫|Dw| ≤ c∫|Dw|.

subproblems.title: Variation bound for 1_F ζ from the Gauss–Green identity (parent step 1; Simon's |D(φ1_E)| ≤ φ|D1_E| + 1_E|Dφ|)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ N. Let D ⊆ R^P be open and F ⊆ R^P Borel. Let μ be a Borel measure on R^P with μ(R^P \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D. Let ν : R^P → R^P be Borel with |ν(z)| = 1 for all z. Assume the Gauss–Green identity (GG): ∫_F div φ dL^P = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ for every C¹ compactly supported φ : R^P → R^P with tsupport φ ⊆ D, where div φ = trace Dφ. Then for every C¹ compactly supported ζ : R^P → [0, ∞) with tsupport ζ ⊆ D, and every C¹ compactly supported g : R^P → R^P with |g(z)| ≤ 1 for all z: |∫ 1_F(z) ζ(z) div g(z) dL^P(z)| ≤ ∫ ζ dμ + ∫_F |Dζ| dL^P. Here |Dζ| is the operator norm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (D F : Set (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ν : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen D → MeasurableSet F → μ Dᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ D → μ K ≠ ∞) → Measurable ν → (∀ z, ‖ν z‖ = 1) → (∀ φ : Euclid P → Euclid P, ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ D → ∫ z in F, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (fderiv ℝ φ z : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) = -∫ z, inner ℝ (φ z) (ν z) ∂μ) → ∀ ζ : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → tsupport ζ ⊆ D → (∀ z, 0 ≤ ζ z) → ∀ g : Euclid P → Euclid P, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ z, ‖g z‖ ≤ 1) → |∫ z, F.indicator ζ z * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (fderiv ℝ g z : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)| ≤ ∫ z, ζ z ∂μ + ∫ z in F, ‖fderiv ℝ ζ z‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 1, which is Simon's estimate |D(φ1_E)| ≤ φ|D1_E| + 1_E|Dφ| in the proof of Ch. 3, 4.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 689–712), written in the dual form the Sobolev step needs.

Fix P, D, F, μ, ν satisfying the hypotheses. Fix ζ ≥ 0, C¹ and compactly supported with tsupport ζ ⊆ D, and g : R^P → R^P, C¹ and compactly supported with |g| ≤ 1. Write div X := trace(DX) and L := L^P = volume. All integrals are Bochner integrals. The hypotheses that D is open and that μ(Dᶜ) = 0 are not used. Measurability of ν only serves to make z ↦ ⟨φ(z), ν(z)⟩ Borel (step 6).

1. Test field. Let φ(z) := ζ(z) g(z). φ is C¹ as a product of the C¹ maps ζ and g. φ vanishes wherever ζ does, so support φ ⊆ support ζ; hence φ has compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ tsupport ζ ⊆ D. By (GG), ∫_F div φ dL = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ.

2. Product rule. By the Leibniz rule (Mathlib fderiv_fun_smul), Dφ(z) = ζ(z) Dg(z) + R_z, where R_z(v) := Dζ(z)(v) g(z), i.e. R_z is the linear map v ↦ a(v) w with a = Dζ(z) and w = g(z) (of rank at most one). The trace is linear, and the trace of v ↦ a(v) w is a(w) (LinearMap.trace_smulRight), so trace(R_z) = Dζ(z)(g(z)). Hence for every z: div φ(z) = ζ(z) div g(z) + Dζ(z)(g(z)).

3. Integrability with respect to L. Dg and Dζ are continuous, since g and ζ are C¹. The trace is a continuous linear functional on the finite-dimensional space of linear maps of R^P, so z ↦ div g(z) is continuous. Hence the three functions z ↦ ζ(z) div g(z), z ↦ Dζ(z)(g(z)) and z ↦ |Dζ(z)| are continuous. All three vanish outside the compact set tsupport ζ, because ζ = 0 and Dζ = 0 off tsupport ζ. So they are L-integrable on R^P, and therefore on F.

4. Rewriting the left side. Since F is measurable, ∫ 1_F(z) ζ(z) div g(z) dL = ∫_F ζ div g dL (integral_indicator). By steps 2 and 3 and linearity of the integral, ∫_F div φ dL = ∫_F ζ div g dL + ∫_F Dζ(g) dL. With step 1 this gives ∫ 1_F ζ div g dL = −∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ − ∫_F Dζ(g) dL.

5. ζ is μ-integrable. K := tsupport ζ is compact and K ⊆ D, so μ(K) < ∞ by hypothesis. ζ is continuous, hence Borel measurable. It is bounded: it is continuous on the compact set K and vanishes outside K. A bounded Borel function is μ-integrable on the set K of finite μ-measure (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). Since ζ = 0 outside K, ζ is μ-integrable on R^P.

6. Pointwise bounds. For every z, |⟨φ(z), ν(z)⟩| = ζ(z)|⟨g(z), ν(z)⟩| ≤ ζ(z)|g(z)||ν(z)| ≤ ζ(z), using ζ ≥ 0, Cauchy–Schwarz, |g| ≤ 1 and |ν| = 1. The function z ↦ ⟨φ(z), ν(z)⟩ is Borel, since φ is continuous and ν is Borel. Also |Dζ(z)(g(z))| ≤ |Dζ(z)||g(z)| ≤ |Dζ(z)| (operator norm, |g| ≤ 1).

7. Conclusion. If |f| ≤ h pointwise with h integrable, then |∫ f| ≤ ∫ h (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le). Apply this with h = ζ for μ (step 5) and with h = |Dζ| on F for L (step 3), together with step 6 and the triangle inequality applied to step 4. This gives |∫ 1_F ζ div g dL| ≤ |∫⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ| + |∫_F Dζ(g) dL| ≤ ∫ ζ dμ + ∫_F |Dζ| dL. ∎
proof_key_steps: Apply (GG) to φ := ζg, which is C¹ with compact support inside tsupport ζ ⊆ D.
Product rule: div(ζg) = ζ div g + Dζ(g), since the trace of v ↦ Dζ(v)g (rank at most one) is Dζ(g).
ζ div g, Dζ(g) and |Dζ| are continuous with compact support, hence L-integrable on F; this gives ∫1_F ζ div g = −∫⟨ζg, ν⟩dμ − ∫_F Dζ(g).
ζ is Borel and bounded and μ(tsupport ζ) < ∞, so ζ is μ-integrable; |⟨ζg, ν⟩| ≤ ζ and |Dζ(g)| ≤ |Dζ| give the bound.

subproblems.title: Symmetric mollification commutes with D and is self-adjoint: ∫ D(η*u)(s) = −∫ u div(η*s) (parent step 2, Fubini part; Simon Ch. 2, 2.5)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ N. Let η : R^P → R be C¹ with compact support and even (η(−z) = η(z) for all z). Let u : R^P → R and s : R^P → R^P be Lebesgue integrable. Write (η*u)(x) = ∫ η(t) u(x − t) dt and (η*s)(z) = ∫ η(t) s(z − t) dt, Mathlib's convolution with lsmul ℝ ℝ and volume. Then ∫ D(η*u)(x)(s(x)) dx = −∫ u(z) div(η*s)(z) dz, where div = trace of the derivative.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (η u : Euclid P → ℝ) (s : Euclid P → Euclid P), ContDiff ℝ 1 η → HasCompactSupport η → (∀ z, η (-z) = η z) → Integrable u → Integrable s → ∫ x, fderiv ℝ (convolution η u (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) x (s x) = -∫ z, u z * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (fderiv ℝ (convolution η s (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) z : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 2: ∇u_ε = (∇η_ε) * u, ∇η_ε is odd, and Fubini. This is the chain ∫ g·∇u^(ε) = −∫ u div(φ_ε * g) in Simon's proof of Ch. 2, Lemma 2.5 (chapter-02.txt lines 543–596), written for a single even kernel η.

Conventions. For f : R^P → R and h scalar- or vector-valued, (f * h)(x) := ∫ f(t) h(x − t) dt = ∫ f(x − t) h(t) dt. This is Mathlib's convolution with L = lsmul ℝ ℝ and μ = volume; the second form is convolution_eq_swap, valid because Lebesgue measure is invariant under translations and under x ↦ −x. Dη denotes the derivative of η.

0. Dη is continuous (η is C¹) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport η. So there is C ≥ 0 with |Dη(y)| ≤ C for all y, and Dη has compact support.

1. Oddness. η(−y) = η(y) for all y. Differentiating y ↦ η(−y) by the chain rule gives Dη(−y) ∘ (−id) = Dη(y), i.e. Dη(−y) = −Dη(y) for all y.

2. Derivative of η*u. u is integrable, hence locally integrable, and η is C¹ with compact support. So η*u is differentiable at every x with D(η*u)(x) = (Dη * u)(x) = ∫ Dη(x − z) u(z) dz (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left, then convolution_eq_swap). The integrand z ↦ Dη(x − z) u(z) is integrable: it is the swapped convolution integrand of the continuous, compactly supported Dη with the locally integrable u (HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_left and ConvolutionExistsAt.integrable_swap). Evaluation at the fixed vector s(x) is a continuous linear map, so it commutes with the Bochner integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply). Hence D(η*u)(x)(s(x)) = ∫ Dη(x − z)(s(x)) u(z) dz.

3. Divergence of η*s. Likewise s is locally integrable, so η*s : R^P → R^P is differentiable with D(η*s)(z) = ∫ A_{z,x} dx, where A_{z,x}(v) := Dη(z − x)(v) s(x). This is (Dη * s)(z) for the bilinear map precompL of lsmul, after convolution_eq_swap; its integrand is integrable as in step 2. View the trace as a continuous linear functional T on the finite-dimensional space of linear maps R^P → R^P (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap of trace ∘ coercion). Then T commutes with the Bochner integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm). A_{z,x} is the map v ↦ a(v) w (of rank at most one) with a = Dη(z − x) and w = s(x), so trace(A_{z,x}) = Dη(z − x)(s(x)) (LinearMap.trace_smulRight). Hence div(η*s)(z) = trace D(η*s)(z) = ∫ Dη(z − x)(s(x)) dx.

4. Fubini. Let H(x, z) := Dη(x − z)(s(x)) u(z) on R^P × R^P. H is a.e. strongly measurable for the product measure L^P ⊗ L^P. Indeed, (x, z) ↦ Dη(x − z) is continuous. s and u are integrable, hence a.e. strongly measurable. Composition with the coordinate projections (x, z) ↦ x and (x, z) ↦ z preserves this (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_fst and comp_snd), so (x, z) ↦ s(x) and (x, z) ↦ u(z) are a.e. strongly measurable on the product. H is obtained from these three maps by the continuous bilinear evaluation (A, v) ↦ A(v), followed by multiplication. Moreover |H(x, z)| ≤ C |s(x)| |u(z)|, and (x, z) ↦ |s(x)| |u(z)| is integrable for the product measure because s and u are integrable (Integrable.mul_prod). So H is integrable on the product, and ∫_x (∫_z H(x, z) dz) dx = ∫_z (∫_x H(x, z) dx) dz (integral_integral_swap).

5. Conclusion. By step 2, the left side of step 4 equals ∫ D(η*u)(x)(s(x)) dx. On the right side, step 1 gives Dη(x − z) = Dη(−(z − x)) = −Dη(z − x). So ∫_x H(x, z) dx = u(z) ∫_x Dη(x − z)(s(x)) dx = −u(z) ∫_x Dη(z − x)(s(x)) dx = −u(z) div(η*s)(z), by step 3. Therefore ∫ D(η*u)(x)(s(x)) dx = −∫ u(z) div(η*s)(z) dz. ∎
proof_key_steps: η even implies Dη(−y) = −Dη(y).
D(η*u)(x)(v) = ∫ Dη(x − z)(v) u(z) dz (derivative of a convolution, swap, evaluation commutes with the integral).
div(η*s)(z) = ∫ Dη(z − x)(s(x)) dx (the trace commutes with the integral, and the trace of v ↦ a(v)w is a(w)).
Fubini on R^P × R^P with the dominating function C|s(x)||u(z)|.
Use oddness to identify the swapped integral with −∫ u div(η*s).

subproblems.title: Mollification does not increase total variation (parent step 2; Simon Ch. 2, 2.5)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ N. Let u : R^P → R be integrable with compact support, and let M ∈ R satisfy |∫ u div g dL^P| ≤ M for every C¹ compactly supported g : R^P → R^P with |g| ≤ 1 everywhere. Let η : R^P → R be C¹ and compactly supported, with η ≥ 0, η even and ∫ η = 1. Then ∫ |D(η*u)| dL^P ≤ M. Here (η*u)(x) = ∫ η(t) u(x − t) dt is Mathlib's convolution with lsmul ℝ ℝ and volume, and |D(η*u)| is the operator norm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (u : Euclid P → ℝ) (M : ℝ), Integrable u → HasCompactSupport u → (∀ g : Euclid P → Euclid P, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ z, ‖g z‖ ≤ 1) → |∫ z, u z * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (fderiv ℝ g z : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)| ≤ M) → ∀ η : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 η → HasCompactSupport η → (∀ z, 0 ≤ η z) → (∀ z, η (-z) = η z) → ∫ z, η z = 1 → ∫ z, ‖fderiv ℝ (convolution η u (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) z‖ ≤ M
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof step 2: the choice s := 1_S ∇u_ε/|∇u_ε| and g := η_ε * s. This is Simon Ch. 2, Lemma 2.5, formula (4) and the chain after it (chapter-02.txt lines 543–596), for a single even mollifier η. The Fubini identity used here is the sibling theorem mollifier_adjoint.

Fix P, u, M and η as in the statement. f*h denotes the convolution ∫ f(t) h(x − t) dt of the Lean statement, L = volume, and div X = trace DX.

1. Let w := η*u. η is C¹ with compact support and u is locally integrable, so w is C¹ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left). η and u both have compact support, so w has compact support (HasCompactSupport.convolution). Let S := tsupport w; S is compact and closed, hence measurable, and Dw is continuous.

2. Gradient. For each x, let ∇w(x) ∈ R^P be the unique vector with Dw(x)(v) = ⟨∇w(x), v⟩ for all v. By Riesz, ∇w(x) = (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ R^P)⁻¹(Dw(x)). The map x ↦ ∇w(x) is continuous, being Dw followed by a linear isometry. Moreover |∇w(x)| = |Dw(x)| (operator norm) and Dw(x)(∇w(x)) = |∇w(x)|².

3. Unit field. Let f(x) := |∇w(x)|⁻¹ ∇w(x), where t⁻¹ is the total real inverse with 0⁻¹ := 0. Thus f(x) = 0 when ∇w(x) = 0. f need not be continuous at zeros of ∇w, and no continuity of f is used. f is Borel measurable. ∇w is continuous by step 2, hence Borel. x ↦ |∇w(x)| is continuous, hence Borel. The real inverse t ↦ t⁻¹ (0⁻¹ = 0) is Borel measurable on R (Measurable.inv), so x ↦ |∇w(x)|⁻¹ is Borel. The product of this Borel scalar function with the Borel field ∇w is Borel (Measurable.smul). Next, |f(x)| = |∇w(x)|⁻¹ |∇w(x)| is 0 if ∇w(x) = 0 and 1 otherwise, so |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Define s := 1_S f, i.e. s(x) := f(x) for x ∈ S and s(x) := 0 for x ∉ S. S is closed, hence a Borel set, so s is Borel (Measurable.indicator). Also |s(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, and s = 0 outside the compact set S, so s has compact support. s is integrable: S is compact, so L(S) < ∞. On S, s = f is measurable and bounded by 1, so f is integrable on S (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). Since s is the indicator of the measurable set S applied to f, s is integrable on R^P (integrable_indicator_iff).

4. Dw(x)(s(x)) = |Dw(x)| for all x. If x ∈ S and ∇w(x) ≠ 0, then Dw(x)(s(x)) = |∇w(x)|⁻¹ |∇w(x)|² = |∇w(x)| = |Dw(x)|. If x ∈ S and ∇w(x) = 0, both sides are 0. If x ∉ S = tsupport w, then w vanishes on a neighbourhood of x, so Dw(x) = 0 (support of Dw ⊆ tsupport w, support_fderiv_subset) and both sides are 0. Consequently ∫ |Dw| dL = ∫ Dw(x)(s(x)) dx.

5. Admissible field. Let g := η*s : R^P → R^P, so g(z) = ∫ η(t) s(z − t) dt. g is C¹ (η is C¹ with compact support, s is locally integrable), and g has compact support (η and s do). η is continuous with compact support, hence integrable, with ∫ η = 1. Since η ≥ 0 and |s| ≤ 1, for all z: |g(z)| ≤ ∫ η(t)|s(z − t)| dt ≤ ∫ η(t) dt = 1.

6. Adjoint identity. η is C¹, compactly supported and even, and u and s are integrable. So the sibling mollifier_adjoint gives ∫ Dw(x)(s(x)) dx = −∫ u(z) div g(z) dz.

7. Conclusion. g is admissible by step 5, so the hypothesis applies to it. With steps 4 and 6: ∫ |D(η*u)| dL = −∫ u div g dL ≤ |∫ u div g dL| ≤ M. ∎
proof_key_steps: w := η*u is C¹ with compact support S := tsupport w.
s := 1_S |∇w|⁻¹∇w (0⁻¹ = 0) is Borel by measurable inversion and product (not by continuity), satisfies |s| ≤ 1, has compact support, is integrable, and Dw(s) = |Dw| everywhere.
g := η*s is C¹, compactly supported and satisfies |g| ≤ ∫η = 1.
The sibling mollifier_adjoint gives ∫|Dw| = ∫Dw(s) = −∫u div g ≤ |∫u div g| ≤ M.

subproblems.title: The Sobolev bound passes from mollifications to the limit (parent steps 3–4; Simon Ch. 3, 4.3 with Ch. 2, 2.5)
subproblems.statement: Let P be a natural number and let p > 0 and c ≥ 0 be real numbers. Write L^P = volume on R^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), |Dw| for the operator norm of the derivative and div g = trace Dg. Assume the Sobolev inequality (S): every C¹ function w : R^P → R with compact support satisfies (∫ |w|^p dL^P)^{1/p} ≤ c ∫ |Dw| dL^P. Let u : R^P → R be Lebesgue integrable with compact support, and let M ∈ R satisfy |∫ u div g dL^P| ≤ M for every C¹ compactly supported g : R^P → R^P with |g(z)| ≤ 1 for all z. Let (η_k)_{k∈N} be C¹ functions R^P → R with compact support such that η_k ≥ 0, η_k(−z) = η_k(z) for all z, and ∫ η_k dL^P = 1. Assume (η_k * u)(x) → u(x) as k → ∞ for L^P-a.e. x. Here (η * u)(x) = ∫ η(t) u(x − t) dt is Mathlib's convolution with lsmul ℝ ℝ and volume. Then (∫ |u|^p dL^P)^{1/p} ≤ c M, with Bochner integrals and the power 1/p written p⁻¹.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (p c : ℝ), 0 < p → 0 ≤ c → (∀ w : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 w → HasCompactSupport w → (∫ z, |w z| ^ p) ^ p⁻¹ ≤ c * ∫ z, ‖fderiv ℝ w z‖) → ∀ (u : Euclid P → ℝ) (M : ℝ), Integrable u → HasCompactSupport u → (∀ g : Euclid P → Euclid P, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ z, ‖g z‖ ≤ 1) → |∫ z, u z * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (fderiv ℝ g z : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)| ≤ M) → ∀ η : ℕ → Euclid P → ℝ, (∀ k, ContDiff ℝ 1 (η k)) → (∀ k, HasCompactSupport (η k)) → (∀ k z, 0 ≤ η k z) → (∀ k z, η k (-z) = η k z) → (∀ k, ∫ z, η k z = 1) → (∀ᵐ x, Tendsto (fun k => convolution (η k) u (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x) atTop (𝓝 (u x))) → (∫ z, |u z| ^ p) ^ p⁻¹ ≤ c * M
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof steps 3 and 4: GNS for the mollifications u_ε, then a.e. convergence along ε_k ↓ 0 and Fatou. This is the Sobolev step of Simon's proof of Ch. 3, 4.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 689–712), with the mollification Lemma Ch. 2, 2.5 (chapter-02.txt lines 543–596). Parent step 2, the bound ∫ |D(η_k * u)| ≤ M, is the sibling theorem mollify_variation. Here the Sobolev inequality (S) and the a.e.-convergent symmetric mollifiers are hypotheses. The parent supplies them from Mathlib: GNS through the sibling gns_real_of_lintegral, and Mathlib's normalized bump functions together with their a.e. convergence theorem. This child uses no import beyond the contract's.

Fix P, p, c, (S), u, M and (η_k) as in the statement. Write L := L^P and w_k := η_k * u.

1. M ≥ 0. The field g = 0 is C¹ with compact support, and |g| = 0 ≤ 1. Its derivative is 0, so div g = trace 0 = 0. The hypothesis gives 0 = |∫ u · 0 dL| ≤ M. Hence cM ≥ 0, as c ≥ 0.

2. The mollifications. Each η_k is C¹ with compact support, and u is integrable, hence locally integrable. So w_k is C¹ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left). Since η_k and u both have compact support, w_k has compact support (HasCompactSupport.convolution).

3. Uniform bound. Fix k. The sibling mollify_variation applies to u, M and η_k. Its hypotheses hold: u is integrable with compact support, M satisfies the variation hypothesis, and η_k is C¹, compactly supported, nonnegative, even, with ∫ η_k = 1. It gives ∫ |Dw_k| dL ≤ M. By (S) for w_k (step 2) and c ≥ 0, (∫ |w_k|^p dL)^{1/p} ≤ c ∫ |Dw_k| dL ≤ cM. Put a := ∫ |w_k|^p dL ≥ 0. Then a = (a^{1/p})^p (Real.rpow_inv_rpow, p ≠ 0), and t ↦ t^p is monotone on [0, ∞) because p > 0. So ∫ |w_k|^p dL ≤ (cM)^p.

4. Lower integrals. |w_k|^p is continuous (w_k is continuous and p > 0) and nonnegative. It vanishes wherever w_k does, since 0^p = 0 for p ≠ 0. So it has compact support and is integrable. Hence ∫⁻ ‖w_k‖ₑ^p dL = ofReal(∫ |w_k|^p dL) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, with ofReal(|t|^p) = ofReal(|t|)^p = ‖t‖ₑ^p). By step 3 this is ≤ ofReal((cM)^p), for every k.

5. Fatou. For L-a.e. x, w_k(x) → u(x) by hypothesis. For such x, ‖w_k(x)‖ₑ^p → ‖u(x)‖ₑ^p, by continuity of t ↦ ‖t‖ₑ and of s ↦ s^p on [0, ∞] for p ≥ 0. So ‖u(x)‖ₑ^p = liminf_k ‖w_k(x)‖ₑ^p for a.e. x. Each x ↦ ‖w_k(x)‖ₑ^p is measurable, since w_k is continuous. By Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le), ∫⁻ ‖u‖ₑ^p dL = ∫⁻ liminf_k ‖w_k‖ₑ^p dL ≤ liminf_k ∫⁻ ‖w_k‖ₑ^p dL ≤ ofReal((cM)^p). The last inequality holds because every term of the sequence is ≤ ofReal((cM)^p) by step 4.

6. Conclusion. |u|^p is nonnegative and a.e. strongly measurable: u is integrable and t ↦ |t|^p is continuous. Hence ∫ |u|^p dL = (∫⁻ ofReal(|u|^p) dL).toReal = (∫⁻ ‖u‖ₑ^p dL).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae). By step 5 and ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal, using (cM)^p ≥ 0, this is ≤ (cM)^p. Raise both sides to the power 1/p, which is monotone on [0, ∞). Since ((cM)^p)^{1/p} = cM for cM ≥ 0 (step 1; Real.rpow_rpow_inv), we get (∫ |u|^p dL)^{1/p} ≤ cM. ∎
proof_key_steps: Testing the variation hypothesis with g = 0 gives M ≥ 0, hence cM ≥ 0.
w_k := η_k * u is C¹ with compact support.
The sibling mollify_variation and (S) give (∫|w_k|^p)^{1/p} ≤ cM, so ∫⁻‖w_k‖ₑ^p ≤ ofReal((cM)^p) for all k.
w_k → u a.e.; Fatou's lemma gives ∫⁻‖u‖ₑ^p ≤ ofReal((cM)^p).
Convert to the real integral and take the power 1/p: (∫|u|^p)^{1/p} ≤ cM.
